mainTopic: What may be bought with מעשר שני money: הבלעה, בן בג בג's דרשה of ״בבקר״, and ריבוי ומיעוט versus כלל ופרט
overview: The amud opens by limiting an earlier ruling: water and salt may be bought with מעשר שני money only when oil was mixed in, and the price of the water and salt was folded into the price of the oil (הבלעה). The גמרא proves that הבלעה is allowed from a ברייתא of בן בג בג, who learns from the פסוק that one may buy an ox with its hide, a sheep with its fleece, and wine with its jug. רבי יוחנן says he would carry the clothes of anyone who could explain the word ״בבקר״ according to בן בג בג. The גמרא shows why: every other word in the פסוק is needed. But once ״צאן״ allows even fleece, an ox with its hide is obvious, and no answer is found. The גמרא then explains the dispute about what may be bought with מעשר שני money. רבי אליעזר and רבי יהודה בן גדיש read the פסוק with ריבוי ומיעוט, which includes almost everything. Other תנאים read it with כלל ופרט, which includes only things similar to the listed items. אביי says fish are the difference between two ברייתות that describe those items differently. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to challenge אביי from another statement of his, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ruling applies only when oil was added
steps.stepSummary: The earlier ruling that water and salt may be bought with מעשר שני money is limited to a mixture that had oil added to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was only needed for a case where he put oil into them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows an earlier ruling so that it fits the rule that plain water and salt cannot be bought with מעשר שני money. It says the ruling only speaks about water and salt that had oil mixed in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water and salt alone are not food that grows from the ground, so they cannot be bought with מעשר שני money. Once oil is added, the mixture includes a real food item. That is how the earlier ruling can permit buying it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was only needed for... (introduces a narrowing of a ruling)
Second tithe; its money may only be spent on food in ירושלים

phrases.english: It was only necessary
phrases.notes: The גמרא is narrowing the ruling from the previous amud down to one specific case.

phrases.english: where he put oil into them.
phrases.notes: The water and salt became a mixture that includes oil, a real food.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא שֶׁנָּתַן לְתוֹכָן שֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a difficulty raised on the previous amud about buying water and salt with מעשר שני money.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might have thought the ruling allows plain water and salt to be bought with מעשר שני money.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling only covers water and salt that had oil added.

steps.title: אביי asks why the oil alone isn't the reason
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges: if oil was added, the mixture is permitted simply because of the oil, so the ruling seems to add nothing about water and salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But let him derive it because of the oil!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי objects to the answer just given. If oil is in the mixture, it is obviously allowed because of the oil, so why would anyone need to say a special rule about water and salt?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is that the answer makes the ruling pointless. Oil may certainly be bought with מעשר שני money. A ruling that only works because of the oil teaches us nothing new about the water and salt.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it (from a simpler reason)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: Said to רב יוסף, according to the standard reading.

phrases.english: But let him derive it because of the oil!
phrases.notes: The oil alone should be enough to allow it, so why do we need a ruling about water and salt?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ מִשּׁוּם שֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer from Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ruling refers to water and salt with oil added.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If oil is present, the purchase is obviously allowed because of the oil, so the ruling about water and salt teaches nothing.

steps.title: He paid for the water and salt inside the price of the oil
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed for a case where the buyer added the cost of the water and salt into the price he paid for the oil (הבלעה).
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it was needed where he paid the value of the water and salt by including it in the price.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי. The new point is that the buyer paid extra for the water and salt, folded into the price of the oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying for the oil itself is obviously allowed. The חידוש is that even the extra money covering the water and salt is allowed, because it was 'swallowed' into the oil purchase. This is the idea of הבלעה.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it was needed for... (introduces a specific case)
Swallowing; folding the price of one item into the price of another

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the buyer is directly buying water and salt with מעשר שני money. He is buying oil, and the cost of the water and salt is hidden inside that one price.

phrases.english: No, it was necessary
phrases.notes: The גמרא answers אביי by pointing to a case where the ruling really does teach us something.

phrases.english: where he paid the value of the water and salt by including it [in the price of the oil].

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא צְרִיכָא, שֶׁנָּתַן דְּמֵי מַיִם וּמֶלַח בְּהַבְלָעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case to show a real chiddush
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed pointless because the oil alone explains the permission.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חידוש is that the extra payment for the water and salt is allowed through הבלעה.

steps.title: Is folding the price in actually allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether one may pay for a forbidden item by folding its price into a permitted purchase.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it permitted by including it in the price?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check the idea it just used. It asks whether הבלעה is really allowed, and this sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 relied on הבלעה, so now that principle must be confirmed. The question is whether money spent on a non-food item becomes acceptable because it is hidden inside a food purchase.

phrases.english: And is it permitted by including it [in the price]?
phrases.notes: The גמרא wants to know where we learn that folding the price in like this (הבלעה) is allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְהַבְלָעָה מִי שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the principle that the answer in Step 3 relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether הבלעה is a valid way to spend מעשר שני money on something that normally may not be bought with it.

steps.title: Yes, proven from בן בג בג's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes and brings a ברייתא of בן בג בג: one may buy an ox with its hide, a sheep with its fleece, wine with its jug, and fermented grape-seed drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. As it was taught: בן בג בג says: 'On oxen' teaches that one may buy an ox along with its hide. 'On sheep' teaches that one may buy a sheep along with its fleece. 'On wine' teaches that one may buy wine along with its jug. 'On strong drink' teaches that one may buy grape-seed drink once it has fermented.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says הבלעה is allowed and proves it from a ברייתא. בן בג בג learns from the words of the פסוק that non-food parts like a hide, fleece, or jug may be bought together with the food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hide, fleece, and jug are not food, yet they may be bought with מעשר שני money when they come together with the food. That is exactly the idea of הבלעה, so it supports Step 3. The last item, תמד, is a slightly different point: a weak grape drink counts as allowed once it ferments and tastes like wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Drink made by soaking grape seeds or skins in water

steps.whatToRemember: הבלעה works: a non-food item may be bought with מעשר שני money when its price is included in a food purchase, like an ox with its hide or wine with its jug.
steps.whyThisMatters: This establishes the general principle of הבלעה in the laws of מעשר שני, which is what allows the water and salt in our case.

phrases.english: Yes —
phrases.notes: This answers the question asked back in Step 4.

phrases.english: and so it was taught: Ben Bag Bag says:
phrases.notes: Introduces the proof from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: 'On oxen' — teaches
phrases.notes: From the פסוק about spending מעשר שני money (דברים י״ד:כ״ו).

phrases.english: that one may buy an ox along with its hide.
phrases.notes: The hide is not food but is included in the price.

phrases.english: 'And on sheep' — teaches
that one may buy a sheep along with its fleece.
phrases.notes: The wool is not food.

phrases.english: 'And on wine' — teaches
that one may buy wine along with its jug.
phrases.notes: The container is included in the price.

phrases.english: 'And on strong drink' — teaches
that one may buy grape-seed drink once it has fermented.
phrases.notes: Once it ferments it tastes like wine and counts as a proper drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין — וְהָתַנְיָא, בֶּן בַּג בַּג אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 4 and supports the answer of Step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The validity of הבלעה for מעשר שני purchases.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of בן בג בג expounding the פסוק in דברים י״ד:כ״ו.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן praises whoever can explain 'on oxen'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says he would carry the clothes to the bathhouse for anyone who can explain how בן בג בג learns his rule from the word 'בבקר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Whoever explains 'on oxen' to me according to בן בג בג, I will carry his clothes after him to the bathhouse.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן comments on the ברייתא just quoted. He says the derivation from 'בבקר' is so hard to explain that he would serve like a servant anyone who could explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן is not rejecting the rule of הבלעה. He is pointing out that the source from the word 'בבקר' specifically is difficult to understand. This sets up the next part of the סוגיא, which will explain what makes it hard.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not making a joke or disagreeing with the הלכה. Carrying someone's clothes to the bathhouse was a servant's job, so he is saying how much he would honor someone who solves this difficulty.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Whoever explains 'on oxen' to me
phrases.notes: The word 'בבקר' specifically is what puzzles him.

phrases.english: according to Ben Bag Bag,
I will carry his clothes after him
phrases.notes: That's something a servant does for his master.

phrases.english: to the bathhouse.
phrases.notes: Shows how much he would honor such a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאן דִּמְתַרְגֵּם לִי ״בַּבָּקָר״ אַלִּיבָּא דְּבֶן בַּג בַּג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the ברייתא of בן בג בג quoted in Step 5 and opens a discussion of its difficult derivation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The derivation of 'בבקר' according to בן בג בג is very difficult to explain.

steps.title: Why רבי יוחנן was puzzled: every word is needed except 'on oxen'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the background to רבי יוחנן's puzzle. Every word in the פסוק has its own job, except בבקר, which seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason for רבי יוחנן's difficulty? All the words are necessary, except for 'on oxen,' which is not necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן found בן בג בג's source so hard to understand. It answers that every word in the פסוק is needed for its own lesson, except בבקר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (דברים יד:כו) lists בבקר, בצאן, ביין, ובשכר. If every other word is busy teaching its own lesson, then בבקר looks like the extra word. That is the background to רבי יוחנן's puzzle about how בן בג בג learns his rule from that specific word. The rest of this passage proves the claim word by word.

keyTerms.meaning: 'On oxen,' a word in the פסוק about spending מעשר שני money

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not necessary' does not mean the word is meaningless. It means the word is not needed for its plain lesson, which is exactly why it stands out.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Why was רבי יוחנן so puzzled?

phrases.english: All of them are necessary
except for 'on oxen,' which is not necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? כּוּלְּהוּ צְרִיכִי לְבַר מִ״בַּבָּקָר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי יוחנן's amazement in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why was רבי יוחנן puzzled by בן בג בג's source?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Every word in the פסוק is needed except בבקר.

steps.title: Asking why the other words are necessary
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for proof that the other words really are each needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are they necessary?
steps.whatsHappening: This short question sets up the next move. The גמרא is about to prove, one word at a time, why each word in the פסוק is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Claiming that every word is needed is not enough; it has to be shown. The answer will be a צריכותא chain. For each word, the גמרא shows that without it we would have wrongly limited the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A proof that each source is needed and cannot be learned from the other

phrases.english: Why are they necessary?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי צְרִיכִי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for proof of the claim made in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does each word in the פסוק teach that the others do not?

steps.title: An ox alone would not teach a sheep with its fleece
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה had written only בבקר, we would allow an ox with its hide, because the hide is part of its body. We would not allow a sheep with its fleece, so בצאן is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if the תורה had written 'on oxen,' I would have said that only an ox may be bought along with its hide, because the hide is part of its body. But a sheep along with its fleece, which is not part of its body, I would say no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins the chain. It shows that 'oxen' alone would not teach us to allow a sheep together with its wool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hide is part of the animal's body and cannot be taken off while the animal is alive. Wool can be sheared off a living sheep, so it seems like a separate item. That is why בצאן is needed to allow the fleece.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (a mistaken first thought)
I would say no (it is not allowed)

phrases.english: For if the Torah had written 'on oxen,'
I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: בָּקָר הוּא דְּמִזְדַּבַּן עַל גַּב עוֹרוֹ,
phrases.english: it is an ox that may be bought along with its hide,
because it (the hide) is part of its body.
But a sheep along with its fleece,
which is not part of its body —
I would say no.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״בַּבָּקָר״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First link in the answer to step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בצאן is needed to permit a sheep with its fleece, which is not part of its body.

steps.title: A sheep alone would not teach wine with its jug
steps.stepSummary: Fleece is still attached to the sheep, but a jug is a completely separate object. So ביין is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written 'on sheep' (along with its fleece), I would have said this is allowed because the fleece is attached to it. But wine along with its jug, I would say no.
steps.whatsHappening: The chain moves forward. A sheep with its wool would not teach us to allow wine together with its container.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wool, even though it can be removed, is still physically attached to the sheep. A jug is not attached to the wine at all. Without ביין, we would not allow buying the jug together with the wine.

keyTerms.meaning: 'On sheep,' a word in the פסוק

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״בַּצֹּאן״ עַל גַּב גִּיזָּתָהּ,
phrases.english: And if the Torah had written 'on sheep,' along with its fleece,
I would have said: it is because it is attached to it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יַיִן עַל גַּב קַנְקַנּוֹ — אֵימָא לָא.
phrases.english: But wine along with its jug, I would say no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״בַּצֹּאן״ עַל גַּב גִּיזָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next link in the צריכותא chain, from sheep to wine.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ביין is needed to permit a jug, which is not attached at all.

steps.title: Wine alone would not teach fermented תמד
steps.stepSummary: A jug is needed to preserve the wine. But תמד that has turned sour is barely a real drink, so the תורה wrote שכר to include it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written 'on wine,' I would have said it is allowed because the jug is what preserves the wine. But תמד that has fermented, which is just sourness, I would say no. So the תורה wrote 'strong drink.'
steps.whatsHappening: The chain continues. Wine with its jug would not teach us to include sour grape-seed drink (תמד), so the word שכר is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The jug is allowed together with the wine because you cannot keep wine without a container. תמד is made by soaking grape seeds or skins in water, and once it turns sour it seems to be just sharp liquid, not real food or drink. The word שכר teaches that it is still included.

keyTerms.meaning: A drink made by soaking grape seeds or skins in water

phrases.english: And if the Torah had written 'on wine,'
I would have said: it is because that (the jug) is its preservation.
But fermented grape-seed drink, once it has fermented,
which is mere sourness, I would say no.
So the Torah wrote 'strong drink.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״בַּיַּיִן״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final forward link, from wine to שכר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שכר is needed to include fermented תמד.

steps.title: Strong drink alone would not teach wine with its jug
steps.stepSummary: Checking the reverse direction: if only שכר were written, we might think it means intoxicating figs from קעילה, which are real produce. Then we would not allow wine with its jug, so ביין is still needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written 'on strong drink,' I would have said: what is strong drink? Dried figs from קעילה, which are real produce. But wine along with its jug, I would say no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now checks the chain in reverse. It shows that שכר alone would not make the word ביין unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צריכותא must work in both directions. If we had only שכר, we might read it as the strong figs of קעילה, which are real fruit and teach nothing about buying a container. So ביין is still needed to allow the jug. Notice that the chain proves the need for every word except בבקר, which is the background to רבי יוחנן's puzzle.

keyTerms.meaning: 'On strong drink,' a word in the פסוק
Dried pressed figs from the town of קעילה, known for being strong

steps.whatToRemember: Each word in the פסוק (בצאן, ביין, בשכר) teaches its own lesson, and none can be learned from another. Only בבקר is never shown to be needed, so it looks extra. That is exactly why רבי יוחנן found בן בג בג's use of it so puzzling.

phrases.english: And if the Torah had written 'on strong drink,'
I would have said: what is 'strong drink'?
Dried figs of Ke'ila, which are real produce.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יַיִן עַל גַּב קַנְקַנּוֹ — אֵימָא לָא.
phrases.english: But wine along with its jug, I would say no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״בַּשֵּׁכָר״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: מַאי שֵׁכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the chain, showing that שכר alone would not make ביין unnecessary.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ביין is still needed, because שכר alone could be read as figs, which are real produce, and would teach nothing about a jug.

steps.title: If only wine were written, a sheep with its fleece would not be allowed
steps.stepSummary: Still checking the reverse direction: ״ביין״ alone would not teach that a sheep may be bought with its fleece, so ״צאן״ is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written only 'wine', we would allow wine with its jug, because the jug keeps the wine safe. But a sheep with its fleece, we would say no. So the תורה wrote 'sheep', to teach that it is allowed even with its fleece.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the reverse check from Step 12. It shows that ״יין״ alone would not teach us about a sheep with its fleece, so ״צאן״ is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The jug is allowed only because it protects the wine, so it serves the food. Fleece does nothing to protect the meat, so we could not learn it from the jug. That is why ״צאן״ must be written separately.

keyTerms.meaning: A jug or barrel for wine
Wool or fleece of a sheep

phrases.english: And if the Torah had written
wine together with its jug,
that is because it is what preserves it.
But a sheep together with its fleece,
I would say no.
So the Torah wrote 'sheep',
to teach that it is allowed even with its fleece.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא יַיִן עַל גַּב קַנְקַנּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the reverse-direction check, moving from שכר to יין and showing that צאן is still needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A jug is allowed because it preserves the wine. Fleece does not preserve anything, so ״צאן״ is needed to allow it.

steps.title: Then why is ״בבקר״ needed?
steps.stepSummary: If a sheep may be bought even with its fleece, an ox with its hide is obvious. So why write ״בבקר״?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need 'oxen'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for the word ״בבקר״. Since ״צאן״ already teaches the bigger חידוש of fleece, an ox with its hide should be obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fleece is less connected to the animal than hide, which is part of its body. If the harder case of fleece is allowed, the easier case of hide must be allowed too. So ״בבקר״ looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why do I need it?', meaning this word seems extra

phrases.english: Why do I need 'oxen'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: ״בַּבָּקָר״ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of Step 13 (צאן allows fleece) to attack the need for בבקר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the word ״בבקר״ in בן בג בג's derivation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fleece is the harder case and hide is the easier case. Once the harder case is allowed, the easier one is obvious, so ״בבקר״ is extra.

steps.title: A suggested answer: without ״בבקר״ we would read ״צאן″ as hide only
steps.stepSummary: Maybe ״בבקר״ is needed so that ״צאן״ is left free to teach fleece. Otherwise ״צאן״ would only teach hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: if the תורה had not written 'oxen', I would have thought a sheep with its hide is allowed, but with its fleece it is not. So the תורה wrote 'oxen' to include its hide, and then 'sheep' is left over to include its fleece.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to save ״בבקר״. This answer will be rejected in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that ״צאן״ by itself could mean either hide or fleece. ״בבקר״ takes care of hide, so ״צאן״ must be teaching something more, which is fleece. In this answer ״בבקר״ is needed only to push ״צאן״ toward fleece.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you will say', introducing a suggested answer that is often rejected
'I would have said', the mistaken first assumption
Is left over or extra, so it can be used to teach something else

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final answer. ״וכי תימא״ signals a suggestion that will be knocked down right away.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: אִי לָא כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״בַּבָּקָר״,
phrases.english: And if you say: if the Torah had not written 'oxen',

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: צֹאן עַל גַּב עוֹרָהּ אִין,
phrases.english: I would have said: a sheep with its hide, yes,
but with its fleece, no.
So the Torah wrote 'oxen' to include its hide.
Then 'sheep' is left over to include its fleece.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: אִי לָא כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״בַּבָּקָר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the קשיא of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra-word reasoning: ״בבקר״ covers hide, which frees ״צאן״ to teach fleece.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without ״בבקר״, ״צאן״ would only teach hide, not fleece.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״בבקר״ is needed so that ״צאן״ teaches fleece.

steps.title: Rejecting the suggestion: the תורה would have written only ״בקר״
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה meant only hide, it would have written ״בקר״ alone. Writing ״צאן״ already shows that fleece is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if the תורה had not written 'oxen', I would not have said that a sheep with its hide is allowed but with its fleece it is not. Because if so, the תורה should have written 'oxen', and 'sheep' would automatically be left over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the answer of Step 15. ״צאן״ by itself would already teach fleece, without any help from ״בבקר״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה only wanted to allow hide, the clear way would be to write ״בקר״, an animal with no fleece at all. Choosing ״צאן״, an animal that has fleece, already shows that fleece is included. So ״בבקר״ is not needed to steer ״צאן״, and the קשיא returns.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For if so', introducing a proof that the idea is wrong

phrases.english: If the Torah had not written 'oxen',
I would not have said:
a sheep with its hide, yes,
with its fleece, no.
For if so, let the Torah write 'oxen',
and then 'sheep' would automatically be left over.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָא כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״בָּקָר״, לָא הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the suggested answer of Step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the idea that ״בבקר״ is needed to free up ״צאן״ for fleece.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If the תורה meant only hide, it would have used ״בקר״ alone. Choosing ״צאן״ already shows that fleece is included.

steps.title: The question returns: ״בבקר″ is still extra
steps.stepSummary: Since ״צאן״ teaches even fleece, ״בבקר״ (hide) is obvious. The question stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since the תורה wrote 'sheep', teaching that even its fleece is allowed, why do I need 'oxen'? Now that a sheep may be bought with its fleece, do we need to be told that an ox may be bought with its hide?
steps.whatsHappening: With the suggested answer gone, the גמרא repeats its question about ״בבקר״ even more strongly. It is preparing for the ending, where no answer is found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses ״השתא... מיבעיא״, an 'if the bigger case, then surely the smaller case' argument. Fleece is the bigger case and hide is the smaller one, so ״בבקר״ adds nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Now that X is true, is Y even a question?', meaning Y is obvious
It may be bought or sold

phrases.english: And since the Torah wrote 'sheep',
to allow it even with its fleece,
why do I need 'oxen'?

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא צֹאן עַל גַּב גִּיזָּתָהּ מִיזְדַּבְּנָא,
phrases.english: Now that a sheep may be bought with its fleece,
is it even a question that an ox may be bought with its hide?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״צֹאן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the answer in Step 16, the גמרא returns to the קשיא of Step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the harder case (fleece) is taught, the easier case (hide) is obvious, so ״בבקר״ is extra.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: no one can explain ״בבקר״ for בן בג בג
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects this unanswered question to רבי יוחנן's saying. He would serve anyone who could explain ״בבקר״ according to בן בג בג.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי יוחנן meant when he said: whoever explains 'oxen' to me according to בן בג בג, I will carry his clothes for him to the bathhouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion without an answer. It shows that רבי יוחנן already knew this word was hard to explain in בן בג בג's approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying someone's clothes to the bathhouse was a job a student did for his teacher. רבי יוחנן means he would treat that person as his רבי, because the problem seems to have no solution. So ״בבקר״ remains unexplained according to בן בג בג.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what he meant when he said', linking the sugya to a known statement
I will carry his clothes, a student's service to a teacher

steps.whatToRemember: Every word in ״בבקר ובצאן וביין ובשכר״ can be defended except ״בבקר״. Since ״צאן״ already allows fleece, hide is obvious. רבי יוחנן admits no one can explain ״בבקר״ according to בן בג בג.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not promising a real reward. He is saying in a dramatic way that the question has no good answer.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא is willing to leave a real difficulty in a derivation unsolved, instead of forcing a weak answer.

phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Yochanan meant when he said:
Whoever explains 'oxen' to me
according to Ben Bag Bag,
I will carry his clothes to the bathhouse.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the unanswered קשיא of Step 17 by quoting רבי יוחנן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ״בבקר״ cannot be explained according to בן בג בג. רבי יוחנן's saying confirms that this difficulty stays unresolved.

steps.title: What is the root of the disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle lies behind the dispute between רבי יהודה בן גדיש, רבי אליעזר, and the תנאים quoted further on.
steps.simpleTranslation: In what do רבי יהודה בן גדיש, רבי אליעזר, and these תנאים mentioned below disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier argument about what may be bought with מעשר שני money. It asks what deeper idea causes these opinions to differ, setting up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we saw what each תנא rules. Now the גמרא wants the reason behind those rulings. It is looking for a difference in how each side reads the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: In what do they disagree? (asking for the root of a dispute)

phrases.english: In what do they disagree

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן גָּדִישׁ וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Gadish and Rabbi Eliezer
and these Tannaim mentioned below?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the open question about ״בבקר״ and returns to the dispute about buying ציר with מעשר שני money.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that divides these תנאים.

steps.title: Two different ways of reading the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן גדיש and רבי אליעזר read the פסוק with ריבויי ומיעוטי. The other תנאים read it with כללי ופרטי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן גדיש and רבי אליעזר learn the פסוק through the method of including and excluding. These other תנאים learn it through the method of general statements and specific details.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two groups use different methods of reading the תורה. It gives the headline here and will explain each method next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words of the פסוק can be read in two ways. ריבוי ומיעוט usually includes a lot, while כלל ופרט usually includes only things like the listed examples. That difference is why the rulings differ.

keyTerms.meaning: Inclusions and exclusions, a method of reading the תורה
General statements and specific details, a different method of reading

steps.confusionAlert: ריבוי ומיעוט and כלל ופרט can look alike, because both have a broad phrase, then a list, then another broad phrase. They are still two different methods, and they lead to different results.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן גָּדִישׁ וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Gadish and Rabbi Eliezer
expound by amplifications and restrictions,
and these Tannaim expound by generalizations and details.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן גָּדִישׁ וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דָּרְשִׁי רִבּוּיֵי וּמִיעוּטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute comes from using ריבוי ומיעוט versus כלל ופרט.

steps.title: Reading the verse as include, exclude, include
steps.stepSummary: The broad phrase includes, the list of oxen, sheep, wine, and strong drink excludes, and the second broad phrase includes again. Include, exclude, include means everything is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן גדיש and רבי אליעזר use inclusions and exclusions. ״You shall spend the money on whatever your heart desires.″ That includes. ״On oxen, sheep, wine, and strong drink.″ That excludes. ״And on whatever your soul asks of you.″ That includes again. When the פסוק includes, excludes, and includes again, it has included everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first method by walking through the פסוק phrase by phrase. It labels each part as including or excluding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under ריבוי ומיעוט, a list in the middle of two broad phrases does not narrow things very much. The second inclusion overpowers the exclusion, so almost everything is included. Only a small amount stays left out, which the גמרא will identify next.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן גָּדִישׁ וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Gadish and Rabbi Eliezer
expound by amplifications and restrictions.
"And you shall give the money
for all that your heart desires" — it amplified,
"for oxen and for sheep
and for wine and for strong drink" — it restricted,
"and for whatever your soul asks of you"
— it amplified again.
It amplified, restricted, and amplified
— it amplified everything.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְנָתַתָּה הַכֶּסֶף בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר תְּאַוֶּה נַפְשְׁךָ״ — רִיבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first method named in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Include, exclude, include means the פסוק includes everything, except for a small exclusion.

steps.title: What does the inclusion cover?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what was included and answers that everything is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did it include? It included everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question to define how far the inclusion goes. It answers immediately that it covers all things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows how wide the ריבוי is. Any food or drink may be bought with מעשר שני money under this method. That leads straight to the next question: if everything is included, what does the middle list leave out?

phrases.english: What did it amplify?
It amplified all things.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי רַבִּי? רַבִּי כׇּל מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the scope of the inclusion described in step 21.

steps.title: What does the exclusion leave out?
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אליעזר, the exclusion leaves out ציר. According to רבי יהודה בן גדיש, it leaves out water and salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did it exclude? According to רבי אליעזר, it excluded fish brine. According to רבי יהודה בן גדיש, it excluded water and salt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the small exclusion is, and the two תנאים give different answers. This is exactly where their earlier argument comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that only one small thing is excluded, but they disagree about what it is. רבי אליעזר excludes ציר, so ציר may not be bought with מעשר שני money. רבי יהודה בן גדיש excludes only water and salt, so for him ציר is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: Under ריבוי ומיעוט almost everything may be bought with מעשר שני money. The argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהודה בן גדיש is only about which single item is left out: ציר, or water and salt.

phrases.english: And what did it restrict?
According to Rabbi Eliezer, it restricted brine,

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן גָּדִישׁ מִיעֵט מַיִם וּמֶלַח.
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Yehuda ben Gadish, it restricted water and salt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי מִיעֵט? לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מִיעֵט צִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ריבוי ומיעוט explanation by naming the exclusion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר excludes ציר. רבי יהודה בן גדיש excludes water and salt.

steps.title: A ברייתא reads the verse as general, specific, general
steps.stepSummary: The other תנאים use כלל ופרט. A ברייתא labels the first phrase as a general statement, the list as specific details, and the last phrase as a general statement again.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these תנאים use general statements and details, as a ברייתא teaches: ״You shall spend the money on whatever your heart desires.″ That is general. ״On oxen, sheep, wine, and strong drink.″ That is specific. ״And on whatever your soul asks of you.″ That is general again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the second method. It brings a ברייתא that reads the same פסוק, but this time with the labels general and specific.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is split up the same way as before. The only difference is the labels: כלל and פרט instead of ריבוי and מיעוט. The next step shows that this change of labels leads to a much narrower result.

keyTerms.meaning: It stated a general rule again

phrases.english: And these Tannaim expound by generalizations and details.
As it was taught:
"And you shall give the money
for all that your heart desires" — a generalization,
"for oxen and for sheep
and for wine and for strong drink" — a detail,
"and for whatever your soul asks of you"
— it generalized again.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי דָּרְשִׁי כְּלָלֵי וּפְרָטֵי. דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the ריבוי ומיעוט method to the second method named in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That these תנאים read the פסוק with כלל ופרט.

steps.title: Only things similar to the listed items
steps.stepSummary: With general, specific, general, we include only items like the details. The details are produce that comes from produce and things that grow from the ground, so everything of that type is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a general statement, a detail, and another general statement, you include only things similar to the detail. Just as the detail is clearly produce from produce and things that grow from the ground, so too everything that is produce from produce and grows from the ground is included.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא applies the כלל ופרט וכלל rule. It defines what all the listed items have in common, and allows only things that share those features.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike ריבוי ומיעוט, this method includes only what resembles the examples. The ברייתא names two shared features: each item comes from something that grew (a calf from a cow, wine from grapes), and each one gets its life from the ground. Anything without both features is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: A general statement, a detail, and another general statement
Things that grow from the ground

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two methods. Include, exclude, include gives almost everything. General, specific, general gives only things like the list.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule makes the list of items that may be bought with מעשר שני money much narrower than under the ריבוי ומיעוט method.

phrases.english: A generalization, a detail, and a generalization

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט.
phrases.english: you may deduce only what is similar to the detail.
Just as the detail is explicitly:
produce of produce, and things grown from the ground,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל פְּרִי מִפְּרִי וְגִידּוּלֵי קַרְקַע.
phrases.english: so too, all produce of produce and things grown from the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלָל וּפְרָט וּכְלָל אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and draws the legal result from the כלל ופרט reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only items that are produce from produce and grow from the ground may be bought with מעשר שני money.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: offspring of the offspring of the earth
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא describes the shared feature differently: the listed items are offspring of the offspring of the earth, so anything of that type is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: just as the detail is clearly the offspring of the offspring of the earth, so too everything that is the offspring of the offspring of the earth is included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a second ברייתא that also uses כלל ופרט. It defines what the listed items share in a slightly different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות agree that only items similar to the list are included. They differ in how they describe the shared feature. One says produce from produce and grown from the ground; the other says offspring of the offspring of the earth. The different wording may include or leave out different items.

keyTerms.meaning: Offspring of the offspring of the earth

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views. The ריבוי ומיעוט method includes almost everything. The כלל ופרט method includes only items like the list, and two ברייתות describe that likeness differently: ״פרי מפרי וגידולי קרקע״ or ״ולד ולדות הארץ״.

phrases.english: And it was taught in another baraita:
Just as the detail is explicitly:
the offspring of the offspring of the earth,
so too, all offspring of the offspring of the earth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: מָה הַפְּרָט מְפוֹרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second ברייתא that uses the same כלל ופרט method but defines the shared feature differently.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything that is offspring of the offspring of the earth may be bought with מעשר שני money.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two descriptions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two ברייתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two ways of describing the listed items actually lead to different results. This short question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said the shared feature is 'פרי מפרי וגידולי קרקע', and Step 26 said it is 'ולד ולדות הארץ'. These two descriptions sound alike. The גמרא wants a concrete item that one ברייתא would include and the other would leave out.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the (practical) difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: 'Them' refers to the two ברייתות from Steps 25 and 26.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical outcome of the two descriptions just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which concrete item is treated differently by the two ברייתות.

steps.title: אביי: fish are the difference
steps.stepSummary: אביי says fish are the difference. One view treats them as grown from the ground, and the other says they came from water.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: fish are the difference between them. According to the one who said 'produce from produce and things grown from the ground,' fish count as things grown from the ground. According to the one who said 'offspring of the offspring of the earth,' fish were created from water.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. Fish may be bought with מעשר שני money according to the first ברייתא, but not according to the second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא counts anything that grows from the ground. Fish qualify because they live in water that rests on the ground and are nourished from it. The second ברייתא needs something born from the earth itself. The פסוקים say fish were created from water, so they are not 'offspring of the earth' and are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
They were created from the water

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a small difference in how we describe the shared feature in a כלל ופרט וכלל can decide whether an entire category, such as fish, may be bought with מעשר שני money.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Fish are the difference between them.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר פְּרִי מִפְּרִי וְגִידּוּלֵי קַרְקַע,
phrases.english: According to the one who said 'produce from produce and things grown from the ground,'
phrases.notes: This is the first ברייתא (Step 25).

phrases.english: these fish count as things grown from the ground.
phrases.notes: So fish may be bought with מעשר שני money.

phrases.english: According to the one who said 'offspring of the offspring of the earth,'

steps.title: Did אביי really say fish grow from the ground?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges whether אביי really holds that fish count as grown from the ground, and begins to quote another statement of his.
steps.simpleTranslation: But did אביי say that fish count as grown from the ground? Didn't אביי say:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's assumption that fish count as 'grown from the ground.' This step is a setup: it opens the challenge, and the contradicting statement of אביי comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 28, אביי's explanation depended on the idea that fish are 'גידולי קרקע.' The גמרא signals that אביי said something elsewhere that seems to contradict this. The actual contradiction has not been quoted yet.

keyTerms.meaning: But did he really say...? (opens a challenge)
But didn't he say...? (brings a contradicting statement)
Things that grow from the ground

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about what אביי meant. It is a קשיא that sets one statement of אביי against another statement of his. The second statement is cut off here and continues on the next amud.
